title: Cold rebuild: Word frequency
summary: Rebuild Word frequency from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Word frequency** in *Sorting, Map and Set*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

code: const b = a.toSorted((x, y) => x - y);
steps.explain: Without a comparator the numbers sort as strings: `"1" < "100" < "25" < "5"`. `toSorted` with `x - y` sorts numerically and leaves `a` alone.

steps.title: Rebuild Word frequency cold
prompt: Write `wordCounts(text)` that counts words using a `Map<string, number>` and returns the result as an array of `[word, count]` pairs, most frequent first, ties alphabetical.
Words are lower-cased and split on spaces; ignore empty strings.
